text: Maci 💋 My POV October 15, 2026 Breckenridge, Colorado Good morning, everyone! ❤️ Well, so much for the weather forecast! Early on they were calling for 4 to 12 inches of snow yesterday, and unless someone secretly shoveled the entire town overnight, I think they missed that prediction by 4 to 12 inches. We did get snow, though, and there's enough on the ground this morning to make everything look beautiful. I'm sitting here with my coffee, looking out at the mountains, and wondering how much longer I can get away with staying in my pajamas. Yesterday was another one of those lazy days, yet managed to fill every hour. Ava FaceTimed us to go over the equipment she's taking to Italy to scan the castle. Edgar helped her double-check everything, and I swear she's more excited about exploring that old place than anyone else. She also flew over to my parents' house because Mom had something special she wanted to give Ava and Spencer. My mother has decided that an 800-year-old Italian castle that's been abandoned for 50 years might have a few unruly residents who haven't quite accepted that they're dead. Mom bought the girls crosses to protect them from evil spirits, just in case. I haven’t seen which ones she chose, but knowing my mother, I wouldn’t be surprised if she’d already had a priest bless them. She absolutely believes in ghosts, and the thought of Spencer and Ava wandering around that castle has her imagination working overtime. Although I do believe we have a friendly ghost who’s rather fond of Edgar, so perhaps I shouldn’t talk. --- The rest of us spent most of yesterday being wonderfully lazy. I worked on our book, Edgar spent some time helping Jenny with work, and everyone seemed perfectly happy staying inside. Except me. I wanted coffee. Yes, we have a espresso machine, but there's a little coffeehouse in town that roasts its own beans, and their coffee is absolutely delicious. Edgar looked outside at the rain, then at me. "You seriously want to walk into town for coffee?" "Yes." "In this weather?" "That's why God invented umbrellas." He shook his head, grabbed an umbrella, and off we went. ❤️ The walk was beautiful, even in the rain. The river was lined with fallen golden leaves, the same ones I photographed and posted yesterday. It was a little sad seeing them scattered everywhere. Autumn never seems to last long enough in the mountains. On our walk back, the rain turned into enormous, fluffy snowflakes. You know the kind that float slowly through the air and make everything look like a Christmas card? I loved it! I went straight into the kitchen and made hot chocolate and cookies for everyone. It was something my mother always did when the first snow arrived in New York. Funny how certain childhood traditions stay with you. I hadn't thought about it in years, but yesterday it just felt right. Then someone suggested Monopoly. Oh, Lord. I warned everyone that I'm competitive. Edgar casually mentioned he hadn't lost a game in five years. Five years! I informed him that I couldn't remember the last time I'd lost either. The funny thing is, Edgar and I have known each other for two years, and even when we were boyfriend and girlfriend, we never played Monopoly together. Jack announced he was pretty good. Mia was mostly interested in the colorful money and choosing her game piece. Jenny wanted to learn, so Edgar started explaining how Monopoly teaches investing, negotiating, and managing money. Twenty minutes later, we were STILL negotiating the rules. Does money go into the middle for Free Parking? Can you trade properties outside your turn? Can you make private agreements? When does the game officially end? I finally told Edgar that if he wanted to hold a board meeting, he should have scheduled one. 😂 We eventually agreed on our house rules and started playing. I figured we'd be finished in an hour or two. Ha! Jenny and Mia were the first to go bankrupt, leaving Jack, Edgar, and me. Then Jack had the misfortune of landing on Edgar's Boardwalk, complete with a hotel. Oh, it was ugly. Jack stared at the board, counted his money, and looked at Edgar like he'd just been personally betrayed. Edgar simply smiled and held out his hand. "Rent's due." And just like that, Jack was bankrupt. Which left Edgar and me. Remember, this is the man who claims he hasn't lost a game of Monopoly in five years. And I couldn't remember the last time I'd lost either. Suddenly, things got very serious. Edgar was sitting there with that irritating little smile he gets when he thinks he's three moves ahead of everyone else. And I'll admit, he had me worried. So I did what any respectable woman facing the possibility of her first Monopoly defeat would do. I recruited Jenny to distract him. She started asking him questions about the castle, his book, and practically anything else she could think of while I worked on negotiating my way out of trouble. Edgar eventually looked at both of us. "You two realize I know exactly what you're doing?" "Doing what?" I asked innocently. By 10 o'clock, neither of us was willing to concede. The snow was falling outside, everyone else was getting tired, and we finally agreed to call it a tie. Edgar insists he was winning. I maintain that he was simply delaying the inevitable. And Jenny? She's been sworn to secrecy about the entire operation. We eventually abandoned our little real estate empire and gathered around the fireplace, telling stories and laughing. Then Mia suggested Two Truths and a Lie. I thought I knew these people. Apparently not. One person claimed they'd once been arrested. Another admitted to sneaking into a wedding reception they hadn't been invited to. And someone claimed they'd gone skinny-dipping in a hotel swimming pool and talked their way out of trouble with security. I'm not telling you which stories were true, but I will say that Edgar's expression during one particular revelation was absolutely priceless. We laughed until my stomach hurt. --- This morning, Edgar was up early, as usual. Jenny joined him for a workout, and I eventually dragged myself out of bed to join them. Nothing like a little competition before breakfast. Jenny is getting stronger, and Edgar has been helping her with her technique. I caught him watching my form during squats and told him that if he had any suggestions, he was welcome to demonstrate. He wisely kept quiet. -- Which brings us to now. We’ve made coffee, and we’re standing by the windows watching the morning light creep across the mountains. We’ve decided to spend the rest of Thursday here, then head down to Denver on Friday morning for the weekend. Edgar has arranged for us to stay at the penthouse, and we're planning some wonderful dinners, dancing, and a little clubbing. I'm especially looking forward to seeing Jenny and Mia experience a few of the places we have planned. But that's tomorrow. Today, I’m perfectly happy staying in Breckenridge, enjoying our whole 1/4 inch of snow, maybe walking into town for another cup of that wonderful coffee, and spending time with these crazy people I love so much. Although I am considering challenging Edgar to a Monopoly rematch. I just need to figure out how to keep him away from Boardwalk. And possibly recruit better accomplices. - Maci 💋 #MyPOV Video by me and #[tool]. We’ve kissed and made up. Six clips and only two errors, both of which I edited out. You’re welcome, Ava.
